subtitle: Lesson 16 · Asynchronous JavaScript

eyebrow: A Promise only ever moves one way

caption: resolve() fulfills the promise; reject() rejects it. Once settled, it can never change again.

code:
getBlockNumber
  .then((block) => console.log("Block:", block))
  .catch((err) => console.error("Failed:", err.message))
  .finally(() => console.log("Done checking."));
caption: then() handles success, catch() handles failure, finally() always runs.

code:
getUser(id)
  .then((user) => getBalance(user.address))
  .then((balance) => getTransactions(balance.account))
  .then((txs) => render(txs))
  .catch((err) => console.error("Pipeline failed:", err));
caption: Each .then() returns a new promise, so dependent steps chain flat instead of nesting — and one .catch() covers every step.
Promise.all waits for every promise to fulfill — or rejects immediately if any one of them fails.
